questions.stem: Employees in my organization believe they are completing tasks significantly faster with AI assistance than they actually are.
Employees frequently use AI to generate materials that look perfect at first glance but require significant human time to fix subtle errors.
Team members often struggle to explain the logic or reasoning behind work they completed with the help of AI.
I have noticed a decline in the ability of entry-level or junior employees to handle basic tasks on their own without using automated tools.
Teams in my organization tend to accept AI-suggested answers over an experienced leader's technical acumen or professional intuition without stopping to double-check them manually.
Work created using AI is frequently redone or heavily rewritten later because it lacked the right context or deep understanding.
If a key process or system in my department breaks down today, very few of my current team members could explain how it works without referencing original automated prompts.
When an experienced employee leaves or a project is handed over, a significant amount of undocumented background context and 'know-how' is permanently lost.
It has become more difficult and time-consuming to train new hires to an advanced level of understanding, despite having access to more digital documentation.
My employees lack the uninterrupted focus time during the workday needed to engage in deep learning or complex problem-solving.
My employees struggle to find the daily time and energy to do their jobs effectively because they are overwhelmed by the volume of digital communications like emails and chat messages.
My employees find it difficult to innovate or think strategically because they are overloaded with managing day-to-day digital tasks and messages.
Employees typically use AI tools to generate initial ideas before doing any independent brainstorming or drafting.
Teams in my organization tend to trust and copy AI-generated answers without actively questioning or verifying the information.
Our organization lacks learning exercises or training that challenge employees to solve hard problems without using technology for scenarios that might occur at work.
